They sent the notice to us and asked that Redwood accept responsibility under the MSA/Order Form indemnity.

Attached is the notice we received (zen_notice_20280416.pdf). Key points:
- Notice dated 2028-04-15 alleging reproduction of Article X from ThirdParty Inc.

- They expect Redwood to accept defense and indemnity per the Order Form language they rely on

Can you confirm:
1) Who at Redwood should be the point of contact for evidence preservation and chain-of-custody requests?
2) Whether Redwood will accept the notice as triggering the indemnity (we're asking for a preliminary acknowledgement within 48 hours)

Please advise on next steps and evidence requirements. If helpful, we can set a short call this afternoon with Acme and our counsel.

Thanks,

Vanessa / Rishi — thanks for the heads up. High-level take: the Order Form indemnity in the active contract (see HubSpot id) does include a third-party IP infringement clause but it is scoped to Customer use of the Service and excludes "customer-provided content" and "outputs that reproduce customer-owned content." The crux is whether the alleged content is: (a) verbatim content from ThirdParty Inc. embedded in the model weights or (b) output that matches a customer prompt that included the copyrighted text.

We will need the following evidence to triage and to preserve our defenses:
- Full redacted chat transcript with timestamps and session IDs (request from Acme via ZenSoft)
- Original third-party DMCA/takedown notice (we have a copy but need the signed version)
- Any customer prompts that contain the copyrighted passage
- Hashes/IDs of the model variant in use, inference logs around the time window, and token-level output snapshot if available

On process / proposed internal approach:
1) Acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and request preservation and the evidence list above (we should not admit liability in the ack).
2) Ask ZenSoft/Acme to route all future third-party communications to "legal@redwood.com" (we'll provide an intake email) and to notify us before any public disclosures.
3) Triage: 5 business days to collect evidence; legal to produce an initial legal assessment within 10 business days.

Proposed redline language (we can send as a tracked change to ZenSoft counsel):
"Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer from third-party claims alleging that the Service, as provided by Redwood, directly infringes a third party's intellectual property rights, provided that: (a) Customer promptly notifies Redwood in writing of the claim; (b) Customer grants Redwood sole control over the defense and settlement of the claim; and (c) Customer reasonably cooperates with Redwood's defense. Redwood shall have no obligation under this Section to the extent the alleged infringement arises from (i) Customer-provided content, (ii) outputs that reproduce Customer-owned content, or (iii) Customer's use of the Service in a manner inconsistent with documented usage guidelines."
I've attached a draft redline for negotiation (proposed_redline_v1.docx). Questions for Sales: can we get a definitive statement from Acme re: how prompts were created and whether any copyrighted materials were uploaded to their workspace?

I'll be available for a call at 3pm PT to run through intake if you'd like.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Amir / ZenSoft counsel —

Thanks for flagging this. Per internal review (legal cc'd), we propose the following mutual action plan (MAP) to ensure timely intake, preserve evidence, and establish next steps. This is an acknowledgement of the notice only and not an admission of liability.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Day 0 (ACK within 48 hours): Redwood acknowledges receipt and requests the evidence checklist below.
- Day 1–5 (Evidence collection): ZenSoft/Acme to provide: redacted chat transcripts (session IDs + timestamps), the original third-party notice, any customer prompts or uploads, and a list of model variant IDs.
- Day 6–10 (Legal triage): Redwood legal will analyze materials and provide an initial assessment and recommendation on defense ownership and next steps (including whether we should assume defense, propose joint defense, or decline).
- Day 11–20 (Negotiation & mitigation): If coverage appears triggered, parties will discuss defense control and settlement authority; concurrently we will propose and test mitigation steps (temporary model variant, targeted prompt-filters).

Evidence checklist (please provide):
1) Full chat transcript (redacted for PII) with session and message IDs
2) Original third-party demand (signed/certified if available)
3) Any customer-provided content or uploads that overlap with the alleged material
4) Approximate timestamps and model variant in use (commit/hash or name)
5) Any internal notes Acme has about user prompts or prompt engineering steps

Contract/redline proposals: attached is a short MAP and a redline excerpt for negotiation. Laura (cc) has proposed language that preserves our right to control defense while signaling cooperation to the customer — we expect to share a tracked redline within 3 business days for ZenSoft counsel's review.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Laura will prepare a short proposed redline (tracked).
- Rishi will pull the signed order form and confirm whether any customer-specific indemnity edits exist.
- I will coordinate a 30-minute triage call with Acme + ZenSoft + Redwood Legal for Friday 4/20 if that works.

Action items for ZenSoft / Acme:
- Confirm you can provide the evidence checklist by EOD 4/20.
- Route all third-party communications to legal@redwood.com and to me for commercial coordination.

We are committed to resolving this quickly and will keep communications tight. Let me know if the MAP above needs adjustment.

Thanks —
